title: Selling arrangements to Elmer Kaiser, Dan Russo and Charlie Strait
summary: Levy sells arrangements to Elmer Kaiser's dance band for about seven years, and writes for Dan Russo and Charlie Strait.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: A very progressive band, yes. A young Chicago kid.

Well, it was, yes, it was a regular dance hall band. It wasn't a jazz band, it was a dance hall band. But when I bought these arrangements up there, they got a big kick out. Then I made some of my own. By studying Duke style and some of the other guys, I began to develop a little bit myself. And I progressed from that straight. And I started to be known as an arrangement.
What were some of the things it is for Clever King? Do you recall that?

Oh, well, I made, I made, I think I made the first arrangement of Rapson in blue around here. First dance arrangement of Rapson in blue. I remember that because we got lots and lots of compliments. And Elmer Kaiser came in and played against us one night and he wanted to know who made the arrangements, so I did. And so I turned around and copied off the score and sold him an arrangement. And then I arranged for him for about seven years. I did some arranging for Giron's Paradise for the business agent, now the union, for Carlin. Yes. And Dan Russo used to have the band at the Age of Water Beach in the Chinese Chopsui place. I made arrangements for him. Then later on, Charlie Strait. That was a band. Yeah, Charlie Strait was a wonderful pianist too. That was earlier really, wasn't it?
Or was it, 25? I was still in the 20s there.
Still in the 20s. I made arrangements for Charlie Strait.
He was active later, but I think his good band was in mid 20s. Yeah, in mid 20s.
